title: Dual-track handshake with fallback crediting for progressive model swaps
author: Maya Patel
release_notes: Introduces a dual-track handshake rollout primitive with session-coherent canary and shadow lanes, plus a fallback crediting mechanism to reserve rollback capacity and prevent unsafe promotions. Includes observability, doc updates, and a rollout playbook.
description:
Context: As part of ENG-2027 we need a rollout primitive that lets product-facing model swaps run two lanes in parallel (a light canary lane + a low-latency shadow lane) while guaranteeing safe, fast rollback without overcommitting capacity. This PR implements a "dual-track handshake" primitive plus a novel "fallback crediting" ledger that: (1) reserves a configurable rollback budget at deploy time, (2) attaches credits to sessions so we can gracefully failover sessions back to the last-known-good variant, and (3) powers a safe, automated rollback playbook when telemetry gates trip.

Motivation: Existing promote/shadow mechanisms either hold too much traffic hostage or allow promotes that leave the system unable to revert quickly under load. The fallback-credit system ensures we never complete a cutover unless we have reserved the rollback capacity and a path to rehydrate session affinity for affected users. This is especially important for Dedicated and Private deployments where capacity is constrained.

Summary of changes (high level):
- runtime/orchestration/dual_track_handshake.go: New handshake coordinator implementing state machine for dual lanes, session pinning, credit reservation, and coordinated promote/revert.
- runtime/orchestration/fallback_credits.go: Fallback credit ledger (in-memory + optional persistent store hooks) and REST endpoints for credit ops.
- console/rollouts/handshake_playbook.md: Playbook for SREs and PS engineers describing how credits are consumed and how to interpret playbook signals.
- telemetry/metrics/handshake_metrics.yaml: New metric definitions and dashboards (reserved_credits, credits_consumed, session_rehydrate_success, lane_mismatch_rate).
- api/rollouts/v1/handlers.go: API surface additions for creating dual-track rollouts and querying credit state.
- docs/deployments/dual_track_handshake.md: User-facing docs and examples for canary/AB/shadow configurations using the new primitive.
- tests/rollouts/dual_track_handshake_test.go: Unit and integration tests covering state transitions, credit accounting, and playbook-triggered rollback.

Checklist: [x] Unit tests added and passing; [x] Integration smoke tests; [x] Documentation (console + user docs); [x] Playbook for on-call; [x] Telemetry dashboards and alerts; [x] Backwards-compatible API (existing promote endpoints still supported).

Commits (summary):
- 1a2b3c4: initial dual-track coordinator state machine and API wiring
- 2b3c4d5: credit ledger implementation + simple in-memory store and REST ops

Changed files (illustrative snippets):

- runtime/orchestration/fallback_credits.go (+230 -8): ReserveCredits(handshakeID, amount) and ConsumeCreditOnRevert(sessionID).
- api/rollouts/v1/handlers.go (+46 -6): POST /rollouts/dual_track -> validates credit policy and returns reserved budget.

Review conversation (high level, condensed into single string):
- Ethan Liu (review): "Nice separation of concerns. Two asks: (1) make credit ledger pluggable so Dedicated customers can persist to K/V store, (2) add a smoke test that simulates a sustained traffic spike during revert."
- Maya Patel (author): "Addressed both: ledger exposes a CredStore interface and we added an integration test that ramps traffic and verifies session rehydration under CPU pressure. See commits 3c4d5e6 and 5e6f7g8."
- Sofia Ramos (review): "Please add more telemetry around credit exhaustion reasons (insufficient_capacity vs policy_block). Also note we should avoid noisy alerting on ephemeral short reverts."
- Maya Patel: "Added credits_* tags and a bounded deduper on the alerting rule; updated playbook with guidance to silence short-duration reverts. See telemetry changes and playbook section."
- Jordan Kim: "CI failed lint on a goroutine leak in tests; good catch. After fix CI green."

CI summary: Initial run: fail (golangci-lint goroutine-check), rerun after fix: pass. Integration pipeline exercise: smoke tests + perf canary with small local cluster: pass. Telemetry dashboard snapshots attached in PR attachments.

Edge cases and known limitations:
- Fallback credit ledger currently relies on eventual persistence for long-lived rollouts; in this PR we wire a simple CredStore interface with an in-memory implementation. A follow-up will add a Dedicated-backed K/V adapter for HA (Linear ENG-2099).
- Session rehydration is best-effort for long-lived websockets; short-lived tokens may not rebind immediately — playbook documents mitigation steps.

Operational playbook (condensed):
1) Create dual-track rollout with reserve_credits=20% (default) via Console or API.
2) Monitor reserved_credits and credits_consumed; if consumed > 50% within first 5 minutes, hold promote and run smoke bisect.
3) If telemetry gates fail (latency SLO or error budget delta), trigger automatic Revert => credits are consumed to rehydrate sessions; if rehydrate_success < 90% within 60s, escalate to on-call and consider capacity-based backout.

Why this is different: instead of a passive shadow or an immediate swap, dual-track handshake treats promote as a two-party commit that requires a rollback budget to be reserved up-front and ties credit consumption to session-level handoff. This reduces the blast radius of failed promotes and gives SREs deterministic playbook actions.

Merge outcome: Squash-merged into main on 2026-02-21 after green CI and approvals from Ethan, Sofia, and Jordan. Backported doc changes to release/v1.8 branch in a follow-up PR.

Related work: See ENG-2027 design doc (link in Linear), follow-ups: ENG-2099 (persistent cred store), PM-189 (console UX for credit tuning).
notes: This PR introduces a new primitive that touches runtime, API and console. The in-memory default is safe but follow-up work required for HA persistence in Dedicated; we recorded that as ENG-2099.
